title: Upstream-deleted WhatsApp message stays in turns, so its pending candidate stays reviewable and its approved claim stays trusted after removal
repro: Ingest 2 messages, approve both candidates (2 verified claims), drop message m1 from the fetcher, re-ingest: claims=2, turns=2. Base ingest only upserts turns, never removes; checkEvidence still matches the stale stored turn. ingest.ts comment says 'Edited/removed source turns must lose trust' but only edits are handled.
fix_direction: Re-ingest should tombstone/remove turns absent from the fetched snapshot (or invalidate candidates whose turn id is absent from the snapshot) in the same transaction as the claim revocation; add a regression test using the repro above. Must land before mount.
resolution: Verified fixed cycle 1: verbatim repro claims 2->1, turns 2->1, pending of deleted msg gone, idempotent on repeat, log holds SHA-256 only.

title: Invalidation is not atomic with the raw turn upsert: if invalidateStaleWhatsAppCandidates fails after base.ingestGroup replaced turns, the approved claim keeps the old quote until a later successful ingest
repro: Approve candidate on 'Scholarship closes Friday.'; edit source to Sunday; make invalidate throw (db blip) after base ingest: claims table still holds the Friday claim (probe printed stale claim text still trusted = true). The quarantine audit does not check claim evidence against current turn text, so nothing reports it.
fix_direction: Run invalidation first against the fetched snapshot, or have the audit also flag claims whose evidence quote no longer equals the turn text.
resolution: Verified fixed cycle 1: failed invalidation leaves marker, audit flags stale quote, repairPendingInvalidations converges and is idempotent.

title: Mutation survivors: materialiser claim status 'verified', excluded/non-approved guards in materialiser, and the three tenant scopes in invalidate/revoke are unasserted
repro: Throwaway-copy mutants: status 'verified'->'needs-review' (SURVIVED, no test asserts the status), personal-excluded guard removed (SURVIVED), non-approved guard removed (SURVIVED), invalidate row.tenantId guard removed (SURVIVED), invalidate find unscoped (SURVIVED), revokeWhatsAppClaim deleteOne unscoped (SURVIVED). The two guards are redundant defence in depth with decide(), but no test calls materializeWhatsAppClaim directly.
fix_direction: Direct materialiser unit test (status, refusals) and a cross-tenant invalidate test with both tenants holding claims.
resolution: Verified fixed cycle 1: all 6 cycle-0 survivors killed by the checker's own mutants.

title: Edit-then-revert leaves an approved candidate with no claim and no way to re-materialise (re-approve returns ok changed:false); admitted gap 5 confirmed
repro: Approve, edit source (claim revoked), revert source, re-ingest: pending re-proposal absent (same id exists as approved), approved rows=2 vs claims=1.
fix_direction: Re-materialise on re-ingest when an approved row's evidence matches again, or mark revoked state in the row (needs schema enum change).

title: POLICY FOR UMESH: approved WhatsApp chat statement becomes claims.status 'verified'; elsewhere 'verified' means hand-verified claim and feeds analytics verified ratio
repro: analyticsModel.ts counts status==='verified'; indexing/session.ts comment treats non-needs-review as hand-verified; materializer.ts sets verified for any approved chat message regardless of sender trust. Sensible only if approval means 'publishable and source-grounded', not 'factually verified'.
fix_direction: Umesh decides: keep verified, or add a distinct review-approved marker/status via schema change. No mount until decided.
resolution: Umesh decided 'mark it verified with soruce as whatsapp'; verified cycle 1: every materialised claim has status verified and source whatsapp from one constant; audit flags a claim lacking it.

title: Read-side quarantine not enforced: raw WhatsApp turns and any pre-existing WhatsApp claims/chunks are served by trusted readers
repro: Non-test readers with no WhatsApp predicate: apps/api/src/ask/ask-arms.ts (lexical turns, tree and vector arms), ask/source-context.ts, search-store.ts, semantic-search/semantic-search-store.ts, grounded-content/reader.ts, store.ts (sessions/turns/claims detail), claims/router.ts via store, transcript-review/planner.ts, packages/index/src/graph/build-graph.ts and routes/graph, packages/ask. Pre-existing on main (old wiring indexes WhatsApp with needs-review claims); not a regression of this lane, which is unmounted.
fix_direction: Follow-up unit: shared predicate excluding sessions whose source.kind is whatsapp-batch unless the row is an approved candidate's own claim, applied to each reader above with planted-text tests per criterion 9; plus purge/audit of already-indexed WhatsApp rows.
verification_note: Verified by checker verdict c404c503 (lane/w17-wire006, candidate 306228cb).

title: Latent: indexSession on a WhatsApp session (non-grounded path) deleteMany({evidence.sessionId}) would also delete approved wa-claim rows; base ingest also resets session status.index to pending on every re-ingest
repro: indexing/session.ts:164 deleteMany by evidence.sessionId; whatsapp/store.ts:168 session replaceOne with index pending. No current caller indexes WhatsApp sessions in the lane; relevant only if a batch indexer or backfill is pointed at them.
fix_direction: Index paths should skip whatsapp-batch sessions.

title: pending-invalidation marker _id is `pending-invalidation:<groupJid>` with no tenant component: with real Mongo's unique _id, a leftover marker of tenant A makes tenant B's ingest of the same groupJid fail on E11000
repro: ingest.ts markerId; the fixture does not enforce _id uniqueness so tests cannot see it. Read of ingest.ts and invalidate.ts log id (`deleted:<turnId>:<at>`, turn ids may also coincide across tenants sharing an owner session hash).
fix_direction: Prefix ids with tenantId and add a two-tenant test on a unique-_id fixture.
resolution: Verified cycle 2: ids are tenant:<len>:<tenant>:..., mutant dropping the tenant prefix killed, boundary-collision pair distinct. Note: two tenants mapping the same owner+group still share a bare session hash (pre-existing base design, ISS-TENANTSRCID-001), outside this lane.

title: An empty upstream snapshot deletes every stored turn and revokes every approved claim of the group without error
repro: Approve a candidate, make the fetcher return [], re-ingest: no error, claims 1->0, turns 1->0 (probe Q4). A misconfigured or transiently empty archiver read is destructive.
fix_direction: Refuse or require confirmation when the snapshot is empty but stored turns exist, or cap the deleted fraction.
resolution: Verified cycle 2: empty snapshot refused with no writes, alert row and kept marker; 10 stored: delete 5 allowed, delete 6 refused; force override only via forceIngestGroup, which the route cannot reach (route uses deps.ingestGroup; wiring.whatsapp exposes only listGroups+ingestGroup). Residual: slow drain is permitted by design (see ISS-013).

title: Deletion log is clean (SHA-256 only) but the decided candidate row of a deleted message keeps its verbatim text and evidence quote
repro: After upstream delete, whatsapp_candidates row for the approved candidate still contains the deleted message text (probe). Also the unsalted SHA-256 of short chat text is dictionary-guessable.
fix_direction: Policy choice: redact text/quote on deleted candidates (schema may need a tombstone), salt the hash.
resolution: Verified cycle 2: after upstream delete, text and evidence quote are redacted on decided rows (approved and rejected); no deleted text in candidates, log, claims or turns.

title: Untested fail-closed guards: removing `if (!messageIds) throw` survives all tests; affected-candidates find tenant scope survives (redundant guard)
repro: Throwaway-copy mutants n8 and s6 SURVIVED; n6 (no revoke in deleted-turn loop) is equivalent because the second loop revokes. n8 matters because a missing snapshot would delete every turn.
fix_direction: Test a fetcher path that yields no snapshot and expect a thrown error with data untouched.
resolution: Verified cycle 2: missing snapshot throws with turns untouched; guard-off mutant killed.

repro: Schema has `origin` only. Recommend adding optional `source` enum [whatsapp] to schema/claims.schema.json with regenerated core types, via the schema-owning unit, so readers and the audit share a typed contract.
fix_direction: Low priority now (only the audit reads it); do it before any reader branches on source.

title: Shrink guard is per-run: a slow drain (1 message per run) is accepted down to a single message; a refusal wedges repairPendingInvalidations (it throws on the first refused group so later groups are never repaired); redaction updateOne tenant scope is an unasserted redundant guard (mutant survived)
repro: 8 messages, deleting one per ingest: 7,6,5,4,3,2,1 all ok, 0 refused. Empty-snapshot refusal then repair throws 'refusing' every call.
